newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 8.

text.p: DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- ROLLS WOOS KAWASAKI FOR AERO PRODUCT

Rolls-Royce yesterday signed up Kawasaki Heavy Industries as its first partner in the development of a new engine for the four-engined 'superjumbo' planned by Boeing and Airbus. Kawasaki will take a 6 per cent share in the estimated 200-300 million pound sterling cost of the project.
-- PFI IS ENLISTED TO PROVIDE TWO WARSHIPS

The Ministry of Defence is hoping to use the Private Finance Initiative to build two roll-on-roll-off ferries to transport tanks and other equipment. Companies are being asked to provide submissions on the 20-year contract. The Ministry has used the PFI for past projects, but has so far retained control of all front-line equipment.
-- POUND RETURNS TO HIGH AS RATES PRESSURE RISES

The average international value of sterling rose from 95.7 to 96.1 yesterday, as expectation of a rise in interest rates grew. Analysts predicted a rise could come as soon as next week after a warning from Bank of England deputy governor that one was needed to control inflation. Sterling is now 4 per cent below its value just before it was forced out of the European exchange rate mechanism in September 1992.
THE TIMES
-- LLOYDS POISED TO SELL MORTGAGE EXPRESS LOANBOOK

Lloyds TSB is understood to be poised to sell it's 1.6 billion sterling loanbook, Mortgage Express. Possible buyers include a Republic of Ireland bank or building society, a UK building society or a foreign bank. Although Lloyds TSB would not discuss the speculation, the view that the disposal will go ahead has been strengthened by the elevation to the Lloyds TSB board of Andrew Longhurst, C&G chief executive.
-- TREASURY FORECASTS MAY GO OUT TO CONTRACT

The Treasury is to look at the possibility of putting its key role as economic forecaster into private hands although any decision will not be made until after the general election. The Treasury is to appoint a consultant by the end of January to study whether it is feasible to contract out forecasting.
-- AUTOLINK WINS 370 MILLION STERLING SCOTTISH ROAD CONTRACT

The first road building project to be carried out under the Private Finance Initiative in Scotland has been awarded to Autolink Concessionaires, a company owned equally by Amey, Sir Robert McAlpine and Taylor Woodrow Construction Holdings. The Scottish Office gave the contract to the three-way consortium after a two-year bidding battle for the 370 million sterling deal, that involves designing, building, financing and operating a motorway link between the M6 at Carlisle with the A74 at Millbank, south of Glasgow.
THE GUARDIAN
-- TROUBLED UNION LOSES SHINE IN MONEY MARKET

Union, the financial services and trading group is planning a company break-up. The company said yesterday it will be unable to pay a final dividend for the last financial year due to tax complications and delays in reaping profits from the sale of software products in Canada. Well-placed sources believe that Union is hoping to boost the value of shares through a series of sell-offs.
-- EC TO CLEAR SCHWEPPES PLANT SALE

The sale of Cadbury Schweppes' soft drinks bottling operation to a Coca-Cola subsidiary is likely to be approved by the European Commission without any special conditions being attached to the 1.2 billion sterling deal. The sale of the venture known as Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages to Coca-Cola Enterprises received unanimous support from an advisory committee yesterday.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- MARJORIE SCARDINO'S PLANS FOR PEARSON

New Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino, who begins the job today, is expected to make a radical difference at the conglomerate, which has attracted City criticism for its 'lack of focus'. Her reputation in her previous job at the Economist Group was as a hands-on, 'intuitive' manager. The troubled CD-Rom manufacturer Mindscape is likely to be an early focus of attention, which analysts predict will be sold rather than saved.
-- SURGE IN EXPORTS LIFTS BRITISH CAR OUTPUT

Figures released yesterday by the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders reveal that the British motor industry exported more cars than it sold at home last year for the first time, with 54 per cent being exported. However, imported cars made up 62 per cent of new cars sold in 1996. The Society expects imported sales to remain high, but predicts that export production will continue to increase.
-- EAGLE STAR TAKES ON VIRGIN WITH CHEAP PENSIONS

Eagle Star, the insurance company owned by BAT Industries, yesterday launched a personal pension plan it claimed was cheaper than any offered by rivals, including Virgin. The new product comes one day ahead of a report by the Personal Investment Authority into the effect of company charges and expenses on financial products.
